reason: Document history row dated August 24, 2022 states ATP can now be used with Amazon CloudFront distributions.
Document history row 'AWS WAF new Challenge rule action option' dated October 27, 2022 says rules can use a Challenge to verify that requests are being sent by browsers.

Row dated April 11, 2023 states the CloudFront maximum body inspection size increased from 8 KB to 64 KB and the CloudFront default is 16 KB; adjacent row confirms it is set in the web ACL configuration.
Row dated August 11, 2022 states a web ACL can now be associated with a Cognito user pool, only in the latest AWS WAF and not in AWS WAF Classic.
What's New quote lists the four tiers and prices for new and existing distributions; the document history row dates the flat-rate plan availability November 18, 2025.
Row dated November 18, 2025 says distributions associated with AWS WAF can subscribe to flat-rate plans with preset service quotas and no unexpected usage charges for that distribution.
Post dated Sep 8, 2025 states 500 MB of CloudWatch Logs Vended Logs ingestion per 1 million WAF requests at no additional cost.
Row dated July 26, 2024 states AWS WAF now limits calls to ListResourcesForWebACL by the accounts in an organization for any single Region.

Quote supports only the propagation time of a few seconds to minutes; the claim's 'new rule or IP set entry in effect in one area and not another' is not in the quote (context mentions rule group rules, never IP set entries), and default_or_max 'max' is not stated.
Row dated June 17, 2025 announces the new console managing web ACLs through protection packs; the console page says a protection pack is not functionally different from a web ACL.
Row dated August 30, 2024 states the minimum request rate for a rate-based rule is now 10, before this 100.
Row dated February 28, 2024 states the window can be 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes and the default is 5, the only option before.
Row dated May 1, 2026 adds quotas for the six listed association types per web ACL with a default of 100 for each.
Quote says only 'some regional resources' on March 7, 2024; the scope qualifier names API Gateway, Cognito, App Runner and Verified Access, which the quote does not state.
Row dated April 28, 2023 states a web ACL can now be associated with a Verified Access instance, only in the latest AWS WAF and not Classic.
Row dated April 11, 2023 states up to 5,000 WCUs per web ACL without a support request and that this limit can't be increased.
Services in Sunset table row lists AWS WAF Classic with announcement October 7, 2025 and end of support October 7, 2026.
Quote states AWS WAF was released in November 2019 and Classic resources must be used with Classic or migrated to the latest version.
Quote states the monthly price with no overage charges regardless of spikes or attacks; the list directly under it includes AWS WAF and DDoS protection.
Under the flat-rate plans heading, quote states a valid web ACL must remain associated under any pricing plan and cannot be removed unless you switch back to pay-as-you-go.
FAQ quote states rules run in all AWS Edge Locations close to end users and blocked requests are stopped before reaching web servers.
Under 'Standard distributions', quote states a single web ACL for each distribution, enabled by associating an existing web ACL or one-click protection in the CloudFront console.
Quote states a web ACL can be associated with one or more CloudFront distributions and, once associated with one, cannot be associated with any other resource type.
Quote states WAF is global for CloudFront but the web ACL and its rule groups, IP sets and regex pattern sets must be created in US East (N. Virginia).
Quote states a Cognito user pool can't be associated with a web ACL that uses the ACFP or ATP managed rule group.
Quote states the console dashboards give near real-time summaries of the CloudWatch metrics AWS WAF collects; context places them on each web ACL's page.
Quotes state the CRS rule group contains rules generally applicable to web applications and to consider it for any AWS WAF use case.
Quotes under the Count behavior state use for general monitoring and testing new rules, confirming settings before switching to allow or block.
Count bullet states it is non-terminating, WAF continues with remaining rules, and in your own rules it can insert custom headers and add labels.
Quota rows state 4 KB for a single custom response body and 50 KB combined for a single rule group or web ACL.
Quote states custom responses for the Block action take precedence over response specifications defined in the protected resource.
Quotes state a custom Block response defines status code, headers and body, and redirection uses a 3xx code with a Location header; context covers rule and default actions.
Quote states the default action must determine the final disposition so it is terminating; the list that follows gives Allow and Block.
Quote states you must set the default action and it applies to requests that pass all rule evaluations without a terminating action.
Quote states to allow most requests set the default action to Allow and add rules that identify requests to block.
Quote matches the claim word for word.
FAQ quote states ACFP is a paid managed rule group that detects and mitigates fake account creation against sign-up or registration pages.
FAQ quote states that as part of API Gateway, AWS WAF can help secure and protect REST APIs.
FAQ quote states that as part of AppSync, AWS WAF can help secure and protect GraphQL APIs.
FAQ quote states ATP is a managed rule group monitoring login page traffic to detect unauthorized access using compromised credentials.
